I don’t know if this will help anyone else, but I am going to put it out there. I have three TBIs, PTSD, chronic pain, and reduced executive function. What that means is that there are days when it is hard to get out of bed, much less be productive. I have had to compensate for that lack of focus by creating systems that cause me to do what needs doing even when I don’t feel like it.

The most important concept is to reduce resistance. You can use this in just about any area of your life. If your issue is overspending, place your credit cards in a safe and take off all cards from your online shopping accounts. If it’s a big hassle to spend, you’re less likely to do so. If you eat out too much, have fully prepped meals at home so it is easier to eat at home than to go to a restaurant. If going to the gym is too hit or miss, have a pair of dumbbells at your bedside so that you can do a quick routine first thing in the morning. Sleep in your gym clothes so when you get up you only need to brush your teeth and go to the gym.

The whole point is make it easier to do what needs doing than it is to do what you shouldn’t. Delete the time wasting apps on your phone so there are no distractions. Keep your desk clean and free of clutter so you can focus on what needs doing. Remove decisions. Remove steps. Remove excuses. And when you’re having one of those days where you don’t feel capable of doing much of anything, lower the threshold for what counts as action.

Don’t tell yourself you have to work out for an hour. Do five minutes.

Don’t tell yourself you have to clean the whole house. Clean one thing.

Don’t tell yourself you have to finish the project. Open it and work for ten minutes.

Make it harder to stay still than to do something. Anything for that matter. Because once you do something, you’ve broken inertia. Action creates momentum. Momentum makes the next action easier. And eventually you realize something important:

You don’t always need to feel motivated enough to act.

Sometimes you just need to design your environment so that action becomes the path of least resistance.

TL;DR: Stop trying to manufacture motivation. Make good behaviors easier, bad behaviors harder, and the first step ridiculously small. Action creates momentum. Momentum is fuel for accomplishment.
